accuracy.evidence: The loop (senses or receptors → sensory nerves → brain decides → motor nerves → muscles) follows BBC Bitesize KS1/KS2 'The nervous system' and the NIH/NIDA 'Brain Power' K–1 materials, where the brain is the control centre protected by the skull. Five senses map to eyes, ears, nose, tongue and skin as in NC Year 1. The speed claim 'faster than a car on a big road' rests on fast myelinated motor fibres conducting at up to about 100 m/s (≈360 km/h, Kandel Principles of Neural Science); it is worded as 'some' messages. Night jobs are true brain jobs: the brainstem drives breathing, the hypothalamus keeps body temperature, and dreams happen in REM sleep. Withdrawal from heat is a spinal reflex, so it is deliberately not used as a brain-decides example, and the adult text says why.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the ideas reported for 5–7 year olds in research on children's ideas of the body (Reiss & Tunnicliffe drawings studies; Primary Science Teaching Trust notes): the heart or tummy is the thinking organ (step 1 predict 'In your heart', tap feedback for chest and tummy, challenge tag heart), hands and legs move by themselves (step 3 predict, mastery m4, challenge tag self), messages travel in blood or bones (challenge tags blood and bone, m2), the brain switches off in sleep (step 5 predict, challenge tags sleep and dream), and wrong sense for an event (wrong-tile feedback in step 2).

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (no flagship lab over 30% similar). 398 Brain Science of Emotions (flagbrain) is about feelings, 171 five senses (flagsense) sorts sense words, 241 naming body parts (flagbody) and 738 Bones & Muscles (flagbones) never show messages. Only this lab draws nerves on a child figure and animates a message dot from each sense up to the brain and from the brain down the spine to the leg, arm or face, plus the sense → brain → muscles ordering of two stories.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners find the boss by tapping parts that each explain their own job first, then watch each sense message travel up to the brain, so 'senses report to the brain' is seen before it is stated. Ordering two different stories (catch a ball, walk to dinner) generalises the loop rather than memorising one example, and dragging the message to the right muscles shows the brain-to-muscle half. The night task shows the brain never switches off. Banners state each rule only after the task is done.

predictions.evidence: Five locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'In your tummy' or 'In your heart' for the boss, 'Your eyes' for a ringing bell, 'Yes, hands think for themselves', 'Slower than a snail' for nerve speed, and 'It switches off' for the sleeping brain. The task that follows disproves each wrong option on screen and the done message says whether the prediction was right.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with tagged wrong answers, each with its own message: heart (the heart pumps, it does not decide), muscle and self (hands do not decide), blood and bone (messages run on nerves), sense (hearing is the ears), ball (the ball cannot tell you anything), sleep and dream (the brain keeps you breathing and warm), hair and tummy (the hard skull is the helmet). Correct answers build a streak.

readability.evidence: Kid text reads at Flesch-Kincaid grade 0.4 (limit 6.5) and adult text at 7.2 (limit 9.5). Canvas words are short: 'Tap the head, chest, tummy, arms or legs', 'Send to: Legs'. The KS1 terms brain, skull, senses, nerves and muscles are each introduced once with a plain picture (a skull like a helmet, nerves as thin wires), and every button says exactly what it does.

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler and the explanation is under 12% similar to every other lesson. Each kid paragraph adds one idea (the brain is the boss in the skull; senses send messages; the brain decides and muscles move; nerves are fast and the brain works at night). The adult text gives curriculum links, the task order, the nerve-speed fact and specific mistakes, including the reflex caveat.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px screenshots in light and dark themes for every step before and after Show me (/workspace/wn-run-20261116-0151/shots/brain). The figure is sized from the column width so the arms never reach the right column; sense, job and night tiles are full half-width and about 44–52 px tall; the loop cards wrap to two lines without clipping; the dark-theme night panel keeps light text on navy.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: every task completes with Show me, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes, no console errors. Every canvas action has a button (Tap: Head, Message from: Ears, Next card: …, Send to: Legs, Pick: Makes dreams), the canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with what is happening and how many are done, and feedback is spoken with c.say.
